title: Sidekick keeps local sessions on the local workspace
intro: A small but pointed fix for Sidekick's terminal routing: when a client has local workspace access, previews now stay on the local workspace instead of being forced through the remote tunnel. Remote-only clients continue to route as before.
highlights: Sidekick prefers local workspace routing when available
Explicit remote agent selections are still respected
Remote-only clients unchanged

title: Hosted workspace files reach the IDE preview
intro: A focused day for Aura's web preview: the IDE can now browse and read the actual files an agent is editing inside a hosted local Harness, closing a long-standing gap between the generic filesystem endpoint and the agent's real workspace.
highlights: File Explorer now reads the live hosted Harness workspace
New server handlers safely proxy workspace-relative reads
Desktop e2e coverage for hosted workspace browsing

title: Command palette, source-control workbench, and hosted Preview routing
intro: Today's nightly lands two sizable interface additions — a global command palette and a native source-control workbench — alongside a server fix that lets the Preview browser reach dev servers running in a separately hosted local harness.
highlights: Global Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette across chats, projects, agents, and actions
New provider-neutral source-control workbench with status, diffs, staging, and commits
Preview browser now tunnels correctly to hosted local harness dev servers

title: Chat transcript stays put while you type ahead
intro: Today's nightly focuses on two long-standing chat annoyances: the transcript scrolling out from under you mid-response, and follow-up prompts disappearing while an answer was still streaming. Both are fixed, and queued prompts now appear inline with a clear "Queued" state.
highlights: Auto-scroll no longer fights you during a streaming response
Queued follow-up prompts stay visible in the transcript with a delivery status

title: Quick Prompts, conversation branching, and hosted Preview land together
intro: A feature-heavy nightly: a new Quick Prompt palette and voice dictation reshape the chat composer, conversations can now branch from any assistant reply, and Preview gains a production-grade hosted Chromium runtime with a remote-localhost tunnel for agent dev servers.
highlights: Quick Prompt palette across the shell
Voice dictation in the chat composer
Branch conversations from any reply
Hosted Chromium runtime for Preview
Remote agent localhost tunneled into Preview

title: Smarter default-browser detection on Desktop
intro: A quiet nightly focused on making Desktop's Advanced settings behave correctly across environments. The single shipped change swaps hard-coded platform checks for capability detection, so browser-related preferences appear only where they actually work.
highlights: Desktop Advanced settings now gate browser options by capability
Same-origin API requests stay local even with a custom host configured

title: Grok 4.6 lands and desktop gains a custom browser path
intro: Today's nightly brings xAI's Grok 4.6 into Aura's managed model catalog with full pricing and reasoning support, and gives desktop users control over which Chromium executable powers managed browsing.
highlights: Grok 4.6 available with 500K context and xhigh reasoning
Configure a custom Chromium executable for managed browsers
New Advanced settings surface for browser executable path

title: Moonshot's Kimi K3 joins the model catalog
intro: A focused nightly today: Aura's model catalog gains Moonshot's Kimi K3, complete with provider routing and accurate cost accounting so sessions on the new model bill correctly out of the box.
highlights: Kimi K3 available in the model picker
Moonshot added as a first-class pricing provider
Cached prompt tokens billed at the correct discounted rate

title: Agents get side questions, recorded skills, and project hopping
intro: Today's nightly is an agent-experience release. Agents can now be moved between projects from the chat surface, desktop workflows can be captured as reusable skills from a short screen recording, and a new ephemeral /btw command lets you ask a one-off side question without polluting the main conversation. Server-side changes tighten how credentialed storage and router requests are validated.
highlights: Switch an agent's project directly from chat
Turn a screen recording into a reusable skill
Ephemeral /btw side questions in any session

title: Model pricing catalog audit and Sonnet 5 introductory rates
intro: Today's nightly focuses on getting model cost accounting right across the board. A time-aware pricing schedule was introduced for Claude Sonnet 5, and a broader audit realigned per-token rates across OpenAI, xAI, Fireworks, and DeepSeek catalogs so cost estimates in the UI stay accurate.
highlights: Sonnet 5 introductory pricing wired into live cost estimates
Full audit of provider pricing tables across OpenAI, xAI, DeepSeek, and Fireworks
LiveRunBanner now uses resolved pricing instead of hard-coded rates

title: Microsoft Edge discovery lands for Windows browser automation
intro: A focused nightly centered on making Aura's embedded browser work out of the box on Windows. The CDP backend now finds Microsoft Edge through the Windows registry, validates configured executables before launch, and surfaces a clear, actionable error when no supported browser can be found.
highlights: Microsoft Edge auto-discovery on Windows via the registry
Actionable browser_launch_failed errors that name Edge, Chrome, and Chromium
Safer CDP launches with pre-flight executable validation

title: Preview/Design modes land, plus universal agent cloning
intro: Today's nightly introduces a split Preview/Design experience for the in-app browser, backed by a new CDP inspection path on the server, and reworks agent cloning into a single flow that targets either local or remote machines. A quick follow-up also tightens the compact Preview toolbar so its controls stay legible in narrow panels.
highlights: Preview and Design modes for the in-app browser
Element inspection over CDP wired end-to-end
Unified agent cloning across local and remote targets
Compact Preview toolbar no longer clips in narrow layouts

title: Clone remote agents into the local harness
intro: Today's nightly introduces a single, focused capability: you can now take a remote swarm agent and spin up a local copy of its configuration without disturbing the original. The change spans a new server endpoint, network client support, and a dedicated UI flow in the Agent Info panel.
highlights: Clone a remote agent into a local one from the Agent Info panel
New server endpoint preserves the source and returns an explicit copy report
Available across Desktop builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows

title: Chat Recall: search your past sessions from the sidebar
intro: Today's nightly introduces Recall, a read-only way to search across your completed chat sessions and jump back to the original message. The feature ships end-to-end across the desktop chat UI, a typed API client, and a new server-side search handler with strict safety and latency guardrails.
highlights: New Recall modal in the chat sidebar for searching past sessions
Bounded, evidence-only server search with per-read and overall deadlines
Partial-result honesty: UI surfaces scanned and skipped session counts

title: Safer worktree isolation and a sturdier desktop harness
intro: Today's nightly tightens two things that quietly shape day-to-day agent work: when Safe Workspace is offered to you, and how reliably the desktop harness and its cloud skills survive real-world restarts. The result is fewer confusing prompts in non-Git folders, a harness sidecar that finds its binary from a signed bundle, and hosted skill sync that actually notices when the remote registry has drifted.
highlights: Safe Workspace now hidden in non-Git folders
Desktop harness resolves its sidecar from the signed app bundle
Hosted skill sync detects and retries drift against the remote Harness

title: Safe Workspace comes to hosted Harness deployments
intro: A focused nightly that extends Aura's Safe Workspace isolation model beyond desktop projects, so hosted-local Web projects running on a capable Harness can finally opt into per-session worktrees — with a clean fallback for older deployments.
highlights: Safe Workspace now runs on hosted Harness
Graceful fallback when the Harness is too old
Spawned child agents inherit the parent's safe worktree

title: Claude Opus 5 lands and safe workspaces isolate parallel agent turns
intro: Today's nightly brings two substantial changes: Aura picks up Claude Opus 5 as its new frontier model across chat, pricing, and bug-report triage, and a new opt-in "safe workspace" mode gives parallel agent sessions their own Git worktree with checkpoint and apply-back semantics so concurrent editing turns no longer race on shared project files.
highlights: Claude Opus 5 available as the new frontier model
Opt-in safe workspaces isolate concurrent agent edits
macOS notifications no longer error on unbundled builds

title: New chat resets cleanly and transcripts stop double-showing prompts
intro: A focused nightly aimed at two long-standing chat annoyances: starting a new chat now reliably clears Council settings on the destination lane, and the transcript projector no longer leaves duplicate optimistic prompts hanging around once the assistant reply has been persisted.
highlights: New Chat clears stale Council state on the fresh lane
Transcript no longer duplicates prompts after a turn completes
Repairs preferences left behind by older builds

title: Chat auto-follow keeps live reasoning in view
intro: A focused nightly centered on how the chat surface behaves while the model is actively thinking. The streaming tail now stays glued to the newest reasoning output, without stealing scroll from you the moment you look back at earlier context.
highlights: Chat stays pinned to live thinking output
Scrolling up now reliably holds your reading position

title: Chat session integrity and dev-loop recovery hardening
intro: Today's nightly focuses on making chat sessions behave predictably end-to-end and keeping the dev loop resilient when tasks or upstream services misbehave. Session identity is now canonical from server to browser, initialization frames no longer race the SSE bridge, and directory outages are cleanly distinguished from dropped LLM streams.
highlights: Fresh chats reliably deliver SessionReady before any turn events
Dev loop auto-promotes pending tasks and recovers from provider stalls
Directory outages no longer masquerade as dropped model responses
Local shadow agents are gated by authenticated ownership

title: Skill delegation, project workspace rebinding, and calmer observability
intro: Today's nightly threads together three focused changes: custom Skills can now target a specific collaborating agent with proper runtime safeguards, project workspaces can be relinked to a local folder on each Desktop machine (including via an agent tool), and the AURA observability workflow settles into a quieter twice-daily cadence.
highlights: Custom Skills can now delegate to a specific project agent
New set_project_workspace tool and Project Settings folder relinking
Observability workflow moves from every-2h to every-12h

title: Project agent mentions land, with safer hosted workspaces and remote availability
intro: Today's nightly centers on a new way to bring specific agents into a project chat with @-mentions, backed by server-side plumbing to keep hosted local workspaces properly isolated. The interface also learns when a remote agent is offline before you hit send, and the release upload pipeline gets more patient with flaky GitHub API responses.
highlights: @-mention specific project agents from the chat composer
Hosted local workspaces no longer leak server-side paths
Remote-agent chat blocks sending when the agent is offline
Release uploader retries GitHub 5xx and malformed responses

title: Project-scoped agent memory lands
intro: Today's nightly introduces per-project scoping for agent memory, giving each agent a cleaner boundary between what it remembers globally and what belongs to a specific project. The change threads a project_id through the chat stack, the harness memory proxy, and the Agent Info panel's Memory tab.
highlights: Scoped memory controls in the Agent Info panel
project_id now routes through chat, tools, and the memory proxy
Self-improvement proposals are attributed to the active project

title: Changelog pipeline slimmed down and gains historical backfills
intro: Today's nightly is a release-infrastructure day focused on the changelog pipeline itself: operators can now safely replay historical dates through the current generator, and a large unused media-publishing workflow was retired to simplify the release path.
highlights: Manual date override unlocks historical changelog backfills
Backfills now run through the current generator, not a stale checkout
Retired ~327 lines of unused changelog media CI

title: Agent continuity, GPT-5.6 models, and a safer macOS relaunch
intro: A feature-heavy nightly: agents gain continuity controls and retrieval evidence in the UI, the model catalog picks up the GPT-5.6 family with a new XHigh reasoning tier, macOS updates now relaunch cleanly after shutdown, and cloud tool callbacks correctly resolve org identity.
highlights: Agent Continuity controls and retrieval evidence in the Memory tab
GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna added with a new XHigh reasoning tier
macOS updater defers relaunch until shutdown completes
Cloud tool callbacks correctly resolve Aura Network identity

title: Aura Web Search launches with Grok 4.5 and quieter task alerts
intro: Today's nightly headlines a new built-in Web Search backed by Aura-funded Brave credentials, alongside a smarter task-completion notifier and a fresh Grok 4.5 entry in the model catalog. Server-side, hosted dev-loop harness calls now carry proper auth end-to-end.
highlights: Aura Web Search ships with tiered quotas and BYOK
Grok 4.5 added to the model catalog
Task completion notifications no longer double-fire
Hosted dev-loop harness auth fixed

title: Native desktop task notifications land on Mac, Windows, and Linux
intro: Today's nightly is focused on a single, substantial shipment: Aura's desktop app can now raise real OS-level notifications when tasks change state, backed by a new notification bridge in the Rust shell and matching preference and toast surfaces in the interface.
highlights: Native task notifications on macOS, Windows, and Linux
In-app toast surface and notification preferences
Permission requested at startup, suppressed in CI

title: Cleaner empty chat state and safer session deletion
intro: Today's nightly tightens two rough edges: the empty chat panel no longer visually collides with the centered input, and the server now consistently hides and fails closed on deleted sessions across chat history, pinning, and pagination paths.
highlights: Empty chat state stops overlapping the centered input
Deleted sessions consistently filtered across chat, pin, and pagination paths
Server fails closed on unsupported session deletes

title: First-run onboarding gets a two-lane choice, plus chat routing that actually remembers where you were
intro: Today's nightly reworks the very first moments in Aura and tightens the chat surface around it. New users now pick between "Just Start" and "Set Up My Agent" instead of being dropped into a six-step wizard, and the chat app learned to preserve, restore, and share concrete session routes across taskbar returns, fresh canvases, and public visitors. The desktop shell also stops flashing hidden windows in CI, and the public chat's free-message limit finally has a real UI.
highlights: New two-lane first-run onboarding replaces the 6-step wizard
Fresh chat canvases now adopt a real session URL after the first send
Taskbar returns preserve the exact chat session route
Public chat has a proper free-limit gate with login CTAs
macOS desktop window shows on launch but stays hidden in CI

title: Workspace access gating and web fallbacks across chat surfaces
intro: Today's nightly centers on making Aura behave predictably when the desktop bridge or a remote workspace isn't fully available: build tools now gate cleanly on workspace access, browse-only remote sessions can't kick off automations they can't finish, and the chat history sidebar gets a brief, reverted experiment in richer row context. E2E onboarding coverage was hardened alongside.
highlights: Workspace-aware gating for automation and build tools
Web sessions no longer dead-end into missing local workspaces
Browse-only remote agents blocked from starting automations
Onboarding eval suite made resilient to Stats overflow

title: Chat-first onboarding and a hardened hosted harness path
intro: Today's nightly reshapes Aura's first-run experience around chat, teaches the web and desktop shells to pick the right entry point for their platform, and lands a substantial reliability pass on the hosted local-harness transport — including auth scoping, autospawn safety, and a runtime-capability API so the UI stops offering local agents it can't actually reach.
highlights: Chat-first, platform-aware onboarding
Desktop shell no longer misdetected as native
Hosted harness transport auth scoped and fail-closed
Public chat transcripts import after sign-in
Web chat stops selecting unreachable local agents

title: Aura-managed Grok routing and a cheaper Grok Build tier
intro: Today's nightly centers on xAI's Grok lineup: chat sessions now flow through Aura-managed xAI credentials, and the Grok Build catalog entry was rebuilt around a cheaper pricing tier with broader model-id aliasing.
highlights: Grok now routes through Aura-managed xAI keys
Grok Build 0.1 relaunched at a lower price
grok-code-fast IDs alias to Grok Build

title: Grok models, Fable 5 returns, and tighter Notion auth
intro: Today's nightly expands Aura's model roster with xAI Grok and brings back Claude Fable 5, while backend work hardens Notion authorization and extends Remote MCP configuration on the server side.
highlights: xAI Grok models and Remote MCP metadata added
Claude Fable 5 restored as a selectable chat model
Notion provider now enforces bearer token auth

title: Sonnet 5 becomes the default, and Notion ships end to end
intro: Today's nightly promotes Anthropic's Sonnet 5 to Aura's default chat model, brings the Notion workspace integration to feature parity with a full tool suite, and quietly fixes a layout bug that was clipping the agent profile card on shorter windows.
highlights: Sonnet 5 is now the default chat model
Full Notion workspace toolset now available to agents
Agent profile card no longer clips on short windows

title: Second Opinion chat strategy and a live leaderboard
intro: Today's nightly introduces a new multi-agent "Second Opinion" chat strategy alongside the existing Council flow, and fixes a long-standing staleness issue in the Feed leaderboard so it stays current while you're looking at it.
highlights: New Second Opinion (Mixture-of-Agents) chat strategy
Feed leaderboard now refreshes live instead of going stale

title: Brave news search starts returning results again
intro: A small but high-impact day: workspace Brave news searches that had been silently coming back empty now return real headlines, backed by a corrected parser and a matching test fixture. The 3D agent profile card also got a layout fix so long agent names no longer collide with the role pill.
highlights: Brave news search no longer returns silently empty results
Agent profile card nameplate redesigned for long names
Regression tests added for both Brave web and news verticals

title: Self-improving agents land with a new Learning tab
intro: Today's nightly is anchored by a single substantial change: Aura agents can now propose improvements to themselves. A new server-side workflow, harness-proxy plumbing, and a dedicated Learning tab in the agent panel turn self-improvement into a first-class, reviewable feature across the stack.
highlights: Agents can now propose self-improvements
New Learning tab in the Agent Info panel
Self-improvement tool wired into agent and instance chat sessions

title: Changelog access lands directly inside Settings
intro: Today's nightly threads a single feature end-to-end: a Change Log entry point in Settings that opens the live, in-app changelog instead of bouncing users out to the web. Follow-up polish trims the embedded view to fit its in-app context.
highlights: Change Log shortcut added to Settings → Updates
In-app changelog modal replaces external web link
Embedded changelog hides Download and GitHub affordances

title: Sturdier streams, smarter pollers, and a refreshed model lineup
intro: Today's nightly is a reliability-leaning release: long-running chat turns are no longer killed by an over-eager watchdog, dead remote agents stop hammering the backend, and the model picker behaves itself when scrolled. Alongside the fixes, three new Fireworks-hosted models land in the catalog and a new server-side usage-signal pipeline begins emitting enriched analytics for completed chat turns.
highlights: Long extended-thinking turns no longer get auto-killed at 60s
Dead remote agents stop flooding the backend with state polls
Kimi K2.7 Code, GLM 5.2, and Qwen3.7 Plus join the model catalog
GPT-5.4 nano calls no longer 400 on unsupported 'minimal' effort

title: Loop Engineering task seeding and restorable archived agents
intro: Today's nightly brings two focused improvements: Loop Engineering runs now automatically come with a backing task so work is tracked from the first kickoff, and archived project agents finally remember their archive state with a clear path to restore them from the project list.
highlights: Loop Engineering runs auto-seed a tracked task
Archived agents persist and can be restored from the project list

title: Skill recovery, manual task fixes, and cleaner analytics
intro: A heavy day of skill-system repair work: user-created skills that had gone missing are now backfilled and recoverable on both server and desktop startup, and the editor finally round-trips every field. Alongside that, manual task creation and chat/browser inputs got QA fixes, web analytics stopped fragmenting by deploy, and release CI gained timeouts to stop runaway probes.
highlights: Orphaned user skills auto-recover on startup
Skill editor round-trips every field again
Manual tasks no longer require a spec
Web analytics reports a stable app_version
Release workflows bounded with timeouts

title: Editable skills, Loop Engineering mode, and a sturdier chat turn
intro: A substantial day for Aura: user-authored skills become editable end-to-end, a new Loop Engineering automation mode lands, and the chat turn gets meaningfully more resilient — from billing pre-flights that survive a cold start to an input bar that no longer eats rapid multiline prompts.
highlights: Edit your own skills directly from the Agents panel
New Loop Engineering automation mode with live status surfacing
Chat turns survive transient billing blips instead of 502-ing
Rapid Enter-then-type no longer drops the second line

title: Live remote agent boot UX and deeper desktop release probes
intro: Today's nightly focuses on making remote agent cold starts feel alive—accurate VM labels, streaming boot logs, and a real provisioning phase indicator—alongside a substantial expansion of desktop release observability covering tool calls, agent-to-agent messaging, and subagent workflows.
highlights: Confidential VMs now report real resources and the correct isolation label
Live VM logs and adaptive polling during agent provisioning
Desktop release probes now cover tools, A2A, and subagents
Context hydration fixed after subagent sessions

title: Resilient chat retries, sharper thinking UI, and harder-edged desktop harness
intro: A reliability-heavy nightly: chat turns and storage writes recover more gracefully from upstream failures, the desktop harness sidecar stops fighting stale processes and inherited env, and the assistant's reasoning surface gets a proper collapsible "Thought for Xs" treatment.
highlights: Failed chat turns now retry on the currently selected model
Compact-retry path rescues chat events blocked by WAF or oversized payloads
Desktop reclaims stale sidecar ports and ignores inherited harness env
Reasoning streams live then collapses to a clickable "Thought for Xs"

title: Analytics rebuild and a sharper feature-health signal
intro: Today's nightly is dominated by two long threads: a ground-up rebuild of Aura's product analytics so True DAU, retention, and reliability numbers are trustworthy across web, desktop, and mobile; and a deep rework of the feature-health system so the status dashboard distinguishes user-facing capabilities from the runtime that actually exercised them. Several follow-up fixes hardened scheduled process runs, image-generation streams, and the desktop release probes that gate every nightly build.
highlights: Analytics rebuilt with a CI contract gate across web, Desktop, iOS, and Android
Feature health split from runtime evidence on the public status page
Scheduled process runs now resolve and propagate the correct model
Image generation streams tolerate sparse progress without false failures

title: A self-healing observability pipeline for Aura
intro: Today's nightly is almost entirely an observability platform push: Aura's status checks gained richer evidence packets, automated source discovery, gated AI-driven repair workflows, and a learning loop that captures lessons across every release. CI guardrails for release history publishing rounded out the day.
highlights: Investigations now ship structured evidence packets with verifier guidance
Gated AI repair loop can auto-dispatch and open PRs for failing checks
Suspect-change detection plus a learning loop across nightly and stable releases
Release history publishing in CI is now guarded against bad runs

title: LLM-powered status investigations land on the public status page
intro: Today's nightly brings a new observability layer to Aura: when status probes fail, an LLM investigator now drafts scoped, evidence-backed diagnoses that are uploaded as release artifacts and rendered directly on the marketing status page. A follow-up fix tightens the prompt against overstated impact and groups repeated troubleshooting cards so the page stays readable when many checks share one root cause.
highlights: LLM investigation reports for failing status checks
Status page renders investigations with grouped troubleshooting cards
Nightly and stable desktop releases now upload investigation artifacts

title: Smoother streaming chat, virtualized transcripts, and a rebuilt input bar
intro: A heavy day for chat performance and polish: the input bar was rebuilt from the ground up to kill typing lag, transcripts now virtualize and paginate, streaming reveals stay in order, and tool markup that used to leak into prose is finally rendered as proper blocks. Behind the scenes, dev-loop runs survive server restarts, swarm VMs expose live logs, and the observability pipeline was reworked to publish a single, trustworthy status snapshot.
highlights: Frame-batched streaming and a rebuilt input bar eliminate typing and reveal lag
Chat transcripts now virtualize and cursor-paginate session history
Tool markup leaks render as proper blocks instead of garbled text
Dev loops reattach across server restarts and keep the task UI live
Per-tool permissions and a fuller generation catalog ship end to end

title: Public site overhaul, agent onboarding wizard, and analytics rescue
intro: A heavy day centered on the public web experience: a full-screen mobile landing, a new glass-styled agent onboarding wizard, a translated marketing surface across 19 locales, and real Terms/Privacy pages. Alongside that, server-side analytics got patched after a silent regression, a feature health status page went live, and chat performance and tone were both quieted down.
highlights: Public marketing translated into 19 locales
New agent onboarding wizard with glass modal UI
Mobile public landing rebuilt around a Creator hero and full-screen menu
Mixpanel analytics restored on desktop and web builds
Aura feature health status page goes live
Chat transcript no longer re-renders on every keystroke

title: Marketing site overhaul, i18n foundation, and agent platform fixes
intro: A sprawling multi-day batch dominated by a top-to-bottom redesign of the public marketing site — new /agents, /code, /os, and /docs experiences with hardware-inspired CSS/WebGL devices, a unified gold accent, and full i18n scaffolding across 20 languages. Smaller but meaningful platform work landed alongside: a logout reliability fix, Telegram MarkdownV2 rendering, remote-agent org healing, richer chat error reports, and Mixpanel OS attribution on server-emitted events.
highlights: Default accent flipped to cyan-green
Telegram replies now render in native MarkdownV2
Web logout hardened so it always clears the session
i18n scaffolding plus 20 locale bundles and a public language switcher
Full marketing site rebuild around a shared device/metal-card kit
New /os whitepaper and /docs CMS surfaces backed by Notes
Chat error blocks now self-report agent, device, and IP context
Mixpanel server events now carry $os for clean OS slicing

title: Pay-per-call LLM access and a new Claude Fable tier
intro: Today's nightly opens up Aura's LLM router to x402-based micropayments, tightens the billing client against unsafe service endpoints, and brings Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 into the managed model lineup.
highlights: New x402 public chat completions endpoint with usage-shaped settlement
Billing client now rejects insecure or private service URLs
Claude Fable 5 available as an Aura-managed Anthropic model

title: Google Workspace lands in Aura: Gmail, Calendar, and a hardened connect flow
intro: Today's nightly is anchored by a single big arrival: first-class Google Workspace integration. Aura now connects to Gmail and Google Calendar through a dedicated OAuth flow, and a late-evening follow-up sweep hardened the save path, preserved OAuth state across edits, and added regression coverage for the new tool catalog.
highlights: Gmail and Google Calendar are now connectable workspace tools
OAuth credentials survive integration rename and edit
Stuck Google reconnect state can now recover
Trusted runtime gained PATCH/DELETE and richer event resources

title: Marketing site refresh, Telegram channel fixes, and a faster, hardened release pipeline
intro: A heavy day of marketing-site work landed a new /code mock desktop and a shared first-screen layout across /code and /agents, while the Telegram channel bridge picked up an IDOR fix and clearer error surfacing. On the platform side, desktop release CI got materially faster and more resilient, macOS DMGs are now notarization-checked before shipping, and a standardized eval-gate framework joined CI to guard chat behavior.
highlights: New /code mock Projects desktop and shared marketing first-screen layout
Telegram channel: IDOR fix, real agent errors, and prod control-plane routing from Desktop
Faster, retry-hardened desktop release CI with macOS DMG notarization validation
Standardized chat-core eval gates and CodeQL coverage added to CI

title: Council mechanics, a public blog, and a smoother Agents↔Projects switch
intro: A big nightly: the council picker and panel grew real mechanism awareness, the agent profile card was split into a 3D nameplate plus a glass spec card, Notes moved to a storage-backed ID model that now powers a brand-new public blog at /blog, and the sidebar gained an Agents/Projects rocker switch that triggered a long performance and animation thread to make it feel instant. Settings also picked up a drill-down Theme section with typography, density, motion, and wallpaper.
highlights: Council combine mechanism is now persistent, visible, and labeled on the panel
Agent profile card split into a 3D nameplate and a frosted glass spec card
New public /blog site backed by ID-based, S3-hosted notes
Agents/Projects sidebar rocker with persistent chat across switches
Expanded Theme settings with typography, density, motion, and wallpaper
Recovery and auto-retry fixes for stalled remote agent chats

title: Computer-use demos, a 3D agent card, and a reshaped desktop shell
intro: A heavy build day on nightly: the /record_demo pipeline grew from a window capture into a framed, agent-driven screen recording with a self-service setup flow; the agent profile became a real WebGL "AURA card" with a flippable persona screen; the authed desktop shell was rebuilt around a rounded screen, a beveled taskbar, and a new chat input pill; and Telegram messaging arrived as a first-class agent channel. Release infra also needed two follow-up fixes to keep Linux builds green.
highlights: /record_demo grows a window-on-background pipeline with computer-use
WebGL agent card with flip-to-persona back face
Telegram channels and agent smart-wallet wired end-to-end
Authed shell redesigned: rounded screen, beveled taskbar, pill chat input
Long remote chat sessions survive idle WS drops via keepalive + reconnect

title: Clearing the path to App Store approval
intro: Today's work is almost entirely focused on unblocking the iOS App Store submission for build 4231. The team shipped the missing pieces App Review flagged — camera and photo permissions, a public support page, in-app account deletion — alongside mobile polish (scrollable settings, a Log Out button, clearer chat guidance) and a fix to keep evals green as the sidekick UI evolves.
highlights: iOS in-app account deletion shipped end-to-end (Apple 5.1.1v)
Camera and photo library permissions added to unblock Take Photo
Public /support page live for App Store Guideline 1.5
Mobile settings now scroll and expose Log Out

title: AURA Council, live subagent threads, and shareable chats
intro: A heavy day centered on multi-agent chat: live subagent threads grew from a clickable card into a fully promptable, persisted slide-over, AURA Council landed end-to-end with N model fan-out and a synthesizer, and assistant messages picked up a Copy/Share/Reload action row backed by a new public share link. Smaller but meaningful work tightened the Sidekick Run pane, added a forced-upgrade gate for stale desktop builds, fixed long-standing sys-admin auth gaps, and shipped an in-app screen-recorded demo command on Desktop.
highlights: AURA Council: N model fan-out with a synthesizer and live member columns
Subagent threads became promptable, persistent slide-overs with shareable history
Public session share links + assistant Copy/Share/Reload action row
Desktop force-upgrade gate when 3+ releases behind
Sys-admin allowlist finally works across login, restart, and Auth0 tokens
In-app /record_demo screen capture on Desktop

title: Model picker overhaul, private bug reports, and a new public marketing shell
intro: A heavy day across the chat experience and the public-facing surface. The model picker grew per-model reasoning effort, credit multipliers, provider grouping, and Gemini support; a new Session Cost view shows what each conversation actually costs; an end-to-end private Bug Reports flow shipped with consent gating and an admin viewer; and the marketing site moved to a centered top nav with a new /code page. highlights: Per-model reasoning effort with credit multipliers in the picker
Session Cost section shows real token spend in chat
Private bug reports with consent gate and admin viewer
Public marketing nav moved to a centered top bar with new /code page

Long-lived sessions counted via hourly heartbeat

Idempotent, fire-and-forget — no impact on response time
